title: Induction of Human Spinal Motor Neurons from iPSCs for ALS Research
author: Setsu, Morimoto, et al.

steps.title: Prepare iPSC feeder‑free culture
steps.instruction: Culture human iPSCs (lines 201B7 and A3411) in feeder‑free conditions using StemFit AK02N medium; keep cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Passage and seed iPSCs
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash gently with sterile 1× PBS (−) twice, then aspirate PBS and dissociate cells with fresh medium containing 10 µM Y‑27632 and iMatrix‑511 by pipetting; count cells and seed 0.3 × 10⁴–1 × 10⁴ cells per well of a 6‑well plate. Immediately after seeding, rock the plate in a cross pattern to distribute cells evenly.

steps.title: Maintain iPSC cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; change medium the day after passage, then change daily or every other day. Use freshly passaged cells at 70 %–80 % confluence and ensure at least one passage after thawing from cryopreservation before differentiation.

steps.title: Induce chemically transitional state (CTraS)
steps.instruction: Replace iPSC medium with 2 mL chemical induction medium containing SB431542, Dorsomorphin, and CHIR99021; change the medium daily for 7 days (Days 1–7) and observe under a microscope for formation of an embryoid‑body‑like state (central elevation of colonies).

steps.title: Perform live‑cell imaging for survival
steps.instruction: Place 12‑well plates with differentiating LMNs onto the Nikon BioStation CT (pre‑condition to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, controlled humidity); set up time‑lapse imaging of a 5 × 5 tile with a 6 h interval using a 10× objective for both phase‑contrast and GFP. Use exposure times from Table 3 (phase‑contrast ≈460 ms, GFP ≈300 ms) and keep fluorescence intensity constant across sessions. Avoid high exposure intensity or prolonged exposure to prevent phototoxicity. Process images with CL‑Quant (background subtraction, cell tracking) and export image sequences and data for analysis in ImageJ or GraphPad Prism. Begin tracking and survival analysis 30 h after mounting the plate.

steps.title: Analyze neurite outgrowth by live imaging
steps.instruction: Mount 12‑well plates with differentiating LMNs onto the pre‑conditioned BioStation CT; set up time‑lapse imaging of six image points per well with a 12 h interval using a 10× objective for phase‑contrast and GFP. Maintain constant fluorescence settings to minimize phototoxicity. Use CL‑Quant for background subtraction and neurite‑outgrowth tracking, quantifying neurite length and cell‑survival duration with a custom single‑cell tracking algorithm. Export high‑quality image sequences and data for further analysis in ImageJ or GraphPad Prism.
